sprint: Home Button — a New Theme No Longer Silently Inherits the Previous Theme's Story-Owned Content
task: The user's own words, right after confirming the crossOrigin freeze fix was finally resolved -- 'it seems to have been fixed. finally.' -- followed immediately by a fresh, distinct, clearly-reproducible bug: 'start working on one theme. press home button. start working on new theme. studio owned changes done on first theme reflects on second theme as well. i checked this with doodle function.' Root cause: the Home button called CreationFlow.start() directly against the SAME live, in-memory AppState -- js/creationFlow.js's _finish() only creates a first page when AppState.slides.length===0, a guard designed for the genuine first-boot case, so a mid-session Home press never actually started a new project -- it silently re-skinned the current one in place via ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme/applyTheme, carrying every Story-owned object (stickers, Doodles, Words edits) straight over onto the newly-picked theme. Fixed by reusing js/publishStudio.js's own proven _makeAnotherStory() precedent for this exact class of problem: ProjectManager.discardSession() followed by window.location.reload(), since AppState is a scattered singleton with no single reset function. Confirmed safe (no data loss) because CreatorProjectStore.upsert() already durably persists a separate My Projects catalog entry per project id, independent of the session-slot key being cleared. Verified via a decisive git-stash A/B Playwright reproduction: the unmodified baseline showed the exact same sticker id leaking from Theme A into Theme B's fresh project; the fixed code showed zero stickers and a genuinely fresh single-page project. Full regression across text_resize_grid_test.js, commitments_test.js, selection_action_strip_test.js, and sync_charm_test.js all pass unchanged; myprojects_test2.js's own pre-existing stale-locator failure was independently confirmed via git-stash to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline. Confined to one click handler in js/app.js.
